title: The Sticky Dog That Invented Velcro
sources: National Inventors Hall of Fame / Velcro Companies: 1941 hunting trip, burdock burrs, microscope, hooks and loops
US patent 2717437 (George de Mestral, granted 13 Sep 1955); name from French velours + crochet; about a decade of development

beats.say: A dog comes back from a hunting trip in the Swiss Alps, covered in burrs. They cling to its fur and won't let go.
Its owner, an engineer named George de Mestral, wondered: why do they stick so well?
So he looked at a burr under a microscope.
It was covered in hundreds of tiny hooks.
And each hook caught on anything with a loop. Fur, hair, even the threads in his clothes.
So George thought: what if we made that? One strip of hooks. One strip of loops.
It took him about ten years to get right. He called it Velcro, from the French words for velvet and hook.
Today it holds shoes, bags, and even astronauts' gear in space. All thanks to one very sticky dog.
